The DAKOTA score aggregates quarterback performance into a single scalar, enabling comparative analysis across players without explicit formulaic definition. It operates under the assumption of stable team dynamics and normalized statistical inputs. The Alpha Role WR metric is a derived dominance index based on target share and red-zone involvement, with approximate values due to visual data legibility issues. This introduces a stochastic element in its application. Yards Before Contact is a direct measure of rushing efficiency pre-contact, used to evaluate blocking effectiveness. All three primitives are subject to temporal drift and data reliability concerns, particularly when timestamps vary ±1–3 hours. Their integration into GSI requires Bayesian calibration for uncertainty propagation and GSE requires them as input states for dynamic roster modeling.
